title: HEXAPOD · Live research poster
mission: Hexapod MKII: from walking to autonomous surveying
description: Progress against the architecture. Evidence is recorded; the team will define the smallest next increments after the repository cleanup.

geometry.label: Canonical detailed direct-drive CAD
geometry.note: User-approved ground truth for all future training. All 1,753 parts and 59 meshes are retained. Nominal motor weight overrides are included; added inertia remains an estimate. Per-leg yaw has a 0.5 mm standoff gap; wider pitch travel permits coupled collisions. Historical videos/checkpoints use their original simplified geometry. Native physics remains unqualified.

checkpoint.label: Historical C-study PPO · 500 updates
checkpoint.qualification: Unqualified historical gait; 0/48 quiet trials pass. New detailed CAD requires native admission.

nodes.title: Draw the survey area
nodes.label: Operator goal
nodes.meaning: An operator chooses the area the robot should cover.

nodes.title: Plan the coverage
nodes.label: Where to go
nodes.meaning: Divide the area into reachable passes while respecting obstacles and the robot’s stopping distance.
nodes.input: Boundary, local map and robot pose

nodes.title: Ask for motion
nodes.label: Forward · sideways · turn
nodes.meaning: A body-frame command combines forward speed, sideways speed and turning rate. Curved paths come from combining them.
nodes.input: A local path and estimated robot pose
nodes.output: Three velocity commands plus a safe stop

nodes.title: Learn the gait
nodes.label: PPO walking policy
nodes.meaning: The policy turns the motion request and recent body/joint observations into targets for all 18 motors.

nodes.title: Sense the surroundings
nodes.label: LiDAR + depth + IMU
nodes.meaning: The Livox Mid-360 and RealSense D455 provide complementary views. Timing, mounts and calibration must make those views agree.
nodes.input: Light, range, images and inertial measurements

nodes.title: Estimate position
nodes.label: No RTK dependency
nodes.meaning: Fuse motion and sensor measurements to estimate where the robot is and how uncertain that estimate is.

nodes.title: Understand the ground
nodes.label: A local height map
nodes.meaning: Maintain a nearby map with height, age, uncertainty and whether a cell is usable for a new foot placement.

nodes.title: Move the robot
nodes.label: 18 RobStride RS05 joints
nodes.meaning: Limit target changes and motor effort, then translate targets through the appropriate robot model.

nodes.title: Train in simulation
nodes.label: Isaac Lab on Spark
nodes.meaning: Many simulated robots collect experience. PPO updates a policy, saves weights and tests that they can be loaded exactly.
nodes.input: Pinned robot, physics, curriculum and correctly versioned policy contract

nodes.title: Try to disprove it
nodes.label: Unchanged acceptance gates
nodes.meaning: Evaluate directions, stops, torques, contacts and smoothness. A good reward curve or attractive clip cannot pass a stage.
nodes.input: Frozen checkpoints and common evaluation cases

nodes.title: Transfer to hardware
nodes.label: Accurate CAD assembly
nodes.meaning: Identify the actual mechanism and actuators, then qualify the complete robot before transferring a simulated policy.
nodes.input: Physical CAD, calibrated motors and tested policy

nodes.title: Collect steady data
nodes.label: The project’s end goal
nodes.meaning: Cover the requested area while holding a steady deck for useful sensor or scientific measurements.
nodes.input: Qualified motion, navigation and survey payload

milestones.title: Walking
milestones.description: The first forward walking policy is the accepted visual benchmark. This establishes the starting point for the new approach.
milestones.gate: The accepted clip is a forward-gait benchmark; it does not qualify every direction or the physical hardware.
milestones.blocker: Historical forward visual comparison accepted; requested-torque failure remains on record.
milestones.question: What does the canonical model need to establish before this comparison can be used?

acceptance.scope: Historical forward visual benchmark only; torque, omnidirectional and hardware qualification excluded.

milestones.title: Omnidirectional movement
milestones.description: Translate in any direction and turn at the same time. Match the forward benchmark’s smoothness and stand still when commanded to stop.
milestones.gate: Numeric gates AND visual quality matching accepted forward Benchmark 1.
milestones.blocker: Canonical batch-standing admission fails; omnidirectional policy qualification remains open.
milestones.question: What is the smallest evidence-producing increment that addresses the current admission blocker?

milestones.title: Terrain and perception
milestones.description: Cross increasingly difficult ground, then use timely sensor information to select safe movement. Retain the flat-ground controller’s capability.
milestones.gate: A frozen terrain envelope, untouched qualification cases and preserved motor/contact limits.
milestones.blocker: Terrain fixtures and sensing prototypes exist; canonical traversal is unqualified.
milestones.question: What is the smallest terrain and sensing envelope worth demonstrating?

milestones.title: Autonomous surveying
milestones.description: Cover an operator-defined area on the accurate robot while maintaining a steady deck for data collection.
milestones.gate: Calibrated hardware and a complete bounded-area mission demonstration.
milestones.blocker: An integrated bounded survey with useful measurements has not been demonstrated.
milestones.question: What smallest region, payload quality and operating envelope would make a useful first survey?

papers.title: CAPS

papers.role: Compare privileged terrain training with realistic perception.

papers.role: Reason about safe paths, known space and the ability to stop.

glossary.meaning: The reinforcement-learning algorithm that updates the walking policy from simulated experience.
The learned function that chooses motor targets from the robot’s observations and motion request.
Saved neural-network weights. A saved checkpoint is not automatically a qualified controller.
What the robot senses about itself: joint positions, motion and orientation.
A training policy allowed to use ideal information that the real robot will not directly have.
Use only sensor information that has actually arrived by the current time, including its delay and uncertainty.

progress.summary: The approved detailed robot passes single-robot standing, but its completed batch screen passes 10/32 replicas. Canonical PPO has not started. Historical walking remains a comparison, with 0/48 quiet trials passing.
progress.definition_policy: Define the smallest useful next increment with James and the two subleads after cleanup. No experiment or contributor assignment is implied by these markers.

facts.title: Canonical standing
facts.text: One robot passes standing. The completed 32-robot screen accepts 10/32; 22 fail measured support, including eight that also fail quiet joint-rate limits. No canonical PPO has run.

metric.window: 16 seconds after 4 seconds settling; original 50 Hz score

facts.title: Recorded contact analysis
facts.text: Both recorded normal-force channels agree on 73 below-bound events. They may share a backend; this does not identify a physical cause or prove buffer completeness.

facts.title: Historical walking policy
facts.text: The 500-update policy retains partial motion but passes 0/48 quiet trials. It does not qualify the canonical robot.
